item.title: How modern payments drive growth and resilience
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · Making Sense — Payments decisions now influence growth, liquidity, and risk — often as much as traditional finance levers. In this episode of Making Sense, co-heads of J.P. Morgan Global Payments Max Neukirchen and Umar Farooq explain how payments became a revenue-enabling capability — and what “trust at scale” requires when clients expect instant, seamless experiences. They cover the move toward real-time rails, the operational demands of always-on infrastructure and the new fraud landscape where threats accelerate with speed. They also detail how data and AI-driven controls help safeguard transactions without adding friction. Looking forward, they discuss intelligent payments and embedded finance, and how blockchain and tokenization — including Kinexys — could modernize cross-border settlement and expand the window for global money movement beyond market hours. This episode was recorded on August 24, 2026.

item.title: Why Oil Prices Are Surging Despite Recovering Supply
item.dc:creator: Goldman Sachs
item.description: Goldman Sachs · Goldman Sachs Exchanges — Middle East crude flows have rebounded, but precautionary buying and portfolio hedging are among the factors keeping prices elevated, says Daan Struyven, co-head of Global Commodities Research and head of Oil Research, on the Goldman Sachs Exchanges podcast. Key takeaways: Precautionary physical buying: Physical buyers are bidding up available crude amid growing downside risks to supply. Portfolio hedging: Bond and equity prices are unusually sensitive to oil prices, prompting institutional investors to buy crude to hedge their portfolios. Supply challenges for refined products: Persian Gulf exports of refined products like diesel and gasoline are still only at around 40% of their 2025 average levels amid damage to refineries and underinvestment in manufacturing. Metal prices may also rise: Struyven expects copper prices to increase another 10% by the end of 2027. He says gold may climb amid central bank demand for the yellow metal. item.description: Bank of America · Global Research Unlocked — In this episode of Must Read Research on Global Research Unlocked, Candace Browning examines the trillion-dollar question facing AI: can returns ultimately justify the enormous investment going into it? We explore the potential $1.5 trillion annual AI subscription opportunity, increasingly crowded investor positioning in Technology and semiconductors, and how AI agents could reshape travel by influencing which flights and hotels consumers see. We also turn to Bitcoin, where a new valuation framework examines whether the asset has been left behind as investors have crowded into AI, and what ETF flows, adoption, and macro conditions could mean for the outlook.
